title: Coin Change
contract: Positive distinct coin denominations may be reused. Return the fewest coins making amount ≥ 0, or −1 if impossible.
brute: if(amount==0)return 0;int best=Integer.MAX_VALUE;for(int coin:coins)if(coin<=amount){emit("Try a final coin","remaining",amount,"coin",coin);int sub=solve(coins,amount-coin);if(sub>=0)best=Math.min(best,sub+1);}return best==Integer.MAX_VALUE?-1:best;
optimal: int[] dp=new int[amount+1];Arrays.fill(dp,amount+1);dp[0]=0;for(int value=1;value<=amount;value++){for(int coin:coins)if(coin<=value)dp[value]=Math.min(dp[value],dp[value-coin]+1);emit("Choose the best last coin from solved smaller amounts","amount",value,"table",dp);}return dp[amount]>amount?-1:dp[amount];
reasoning: Try every possible final coin and recursively solve the remaining amount.
Positive coins ensure the recurrence refers only to smaller amounts, so fill the table in ascending amount order.
Use a sentinel larger than any feasible coin count. Greedily taking the largest coin fails for arbitrary denominations, for example [1,3,4] at amount 6.
complexity: O(m^A) loose upper bound, O(A) stack
